title: Performance: Replace `strings.ToLower() ==` with `strings.EqualFold()` to prevent unnecessary allocations
body:
<!--
Thank you for reporting an issue.

This issue tracker is for bugs and issues found within Podman.
Please fill in as much of the template below as you're able.
-->

### Describe the issue

In a few places across the codebase, there are case-insensitive string comparisons being performed using `strings.ToLower(x) == "..."`.

For example:
```go
if strings.ToLower(splitRestart[0]) == "never" {
```
This pattern allocates a brand new, fully lowercased string on the heap solely for the purpose of the comparison. In hot paths like CLI argument parsing or configuration evaluation, this causes unnecessary garbage collection and memory overhead.


### Expected Behavior
These checks should be replaced with strings.EqualFold(a, b), which performs the case-insensitive comparison directly in-place without making any heap allocations.

```go
if strings.EqualFold(splitRestart[0], "never") {
```

This is a standard Go performance best practice. I would be happy to submit a quick Pull Request to clean these up if maintainers agree!
